key_insight: LES grid resolution changes predicted hurricane winds and turbulence, producing distinct aeroelastic responses in an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: High-resolution hurricane inflow information can improve extreme-load predictions and support wind turbine design in cyclone-prone regions.
method: Simulate Hurricane Laura (2020) using large-eddy simulation.
Compare grid spacings of 55.55 m, 25 m, and 10 m.
Use LES inflow directly in aeroelastic simulations of an idling turbine.
evidence_signal: Across three grid resolutions, the simulations showed significant differences in mean winds and turbulence structures, with corresponding differences in turbine response.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish grid convergence or quantify load differences; storm-relative location effects and comparisons with design practices are deferred to Part II.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
